## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Primitives
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Multi-dimensional arrays
//  - Tuples

//==
// # Multi-dimensional arrays
//
// Immutable, eagerly-or-lazily backed ordered collections. The compiler maps
// indexing syntax to At.
//
// The one-dimensional `Array<T>` moved to `primitives.plato` (plato-367): it is a
// name the compiler assumes. The rank-2 and rank-3 forms below are NOT - they are
// ordinary types whose shape is their declaration, so they stay `type`.
//
// Both carry an HONEST LAYOUT as of plato-378: a flat row-major `Elements` store
// plus the extents. They used to be opaque and field-less, which is why their
// construction and traversal had to be host intrinsics — the one documented
// exception to the primitive-only rule in `intrinsics.library.plato`. With a
// declared shape the exception is gone: `MakeArray2D`, `At`, `Column`, `Row`,
// `Map`, `Slices` and `CartesianProduct` are ordinary Plato bodies in
// `primitives.library.plato`.
//
// The extent fields are named for the interface obligations they discharge
// (`ColumnCount` / `RowCount` / `LayerCount` on IIndexable2D / IIndexable3D), so a
// field satisfies each one directly rather than needing a library function keyed
// on the type's own parameter — the shape plato-376 says can never bind.
//
// Row-major throughout, matching `Collections.FlattenIndex`:
// index = (layer * RowCount + row) * ColumnCount + column.

// An immutable collection addressed by column and row.
type Array2D<T>
    implements IIndexable2D<T>
{
    Elements: Array<T>;
    ColumnCount: Integer;
    RowCount: Integer;
}

// An immutable collection addressed by column, row, and layer.
type Array3D<T>
    implements IIndexable3D<T>
{
    Elements: Array<T>;
    ColumnCount: Integer;
    RowCount: Integer;
    LayerCount: Integer;
}

//==
// # Tuples
//
// Anonymous product types (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuple). Tuple literals
// construct them: (a, b) is a Tuple2. The compiler synthesizes a TupleN
// constructor for every type with N fields, and supports at most 10-field
// tuples — so no type may exceed 10 fields.

type Tuple2<T0, T1> { X0: T0; X1: T1; }
type Tuple3<T0, T1, T2> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; }
type Tuple4<T0, T1, T2, T3> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; }
type Tuple5<T0, T1, T2, T3, T4> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; X4: T4; }
type Tuple6<T0, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; X4: T4; X5: T5; }
type Tuple7<T0, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; X4: T4; X5: T5; X6: T6; }
type Tuple8<T0, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; X4: T4; X5: T5; X6: T6; X7: T7; }
type Tuple9<T0, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; X4: T4; X5: T5; X6: T6; X7: T7; X8: T8; }
type Tuple10<T0, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9> { X0: T0; X1: T1; X2: T2; X3: T3; X4: T4; X5: T5; X6: T6; X7: T7; X8: T8; X9: T9; }
```
